children: CFO Bret Johnsen said the company has gained greater conviction that it can reach a $100B annual revenue run rate, underscoring the rapid growth expectations for Elon Musk’s space and satellite-internet company.

Johnsen said at a Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference that the company had signed a new deal to provide AI computing power to an undisclosed customer, worth $1.11B a month beginning in December. The contract represents about $13B in annualized revenue. He added that the deal gives SpaceX “even more conviction” around reaching the $100B annual revenue run rate.

He also discussed SpaceX's plans to expand its terrestrial AI-computing capacity, saying the company expects to have a little over 2 gigawatts deployed by the end of 2026 and is targeting 5 GW to 10 GW of capacity in 2027.
Johnsen said power availability is increasingly becoming a constraint for terrestrial AI infrastructure, which is one reason SpaceX is exploring orbital computing as a longer-term opportunity.
Running the numbers, ARR target is an annual run rate based on monthly revenue multiplied by 12, rather than $100B of reported revenue for 2026. SpaceX
would need to generate about $8.3B a month to reach that pace. The satellite operator reported $7.8B in Q2 revenue, or about $2.6B a month, meaning monthly revenue would need to more than triple.
The current deals include a $6.7B cloud-services agreement ramping in October and an AI hosting deal worth $1.11B a month starting in December. Its AI compute deals with Google
are already generating more than $2B a month.
The $100B figure depends on how quickly these deals ramp, with delays or slower growth potentially keeping SpaceX
Johnsen had previously said the company's AI infrastructure spending can have a payback period of less than a year because of the contracts it has secured to lease computing capacity.

title: SpaceX CFO gains ‘even more conviction’ in $100B ARR target
